model: iO (Bluetooth model with OLED screen, as torn down by iFixit in October 2020)
notes: Covers the Oral-B iO as torn down in October 2020; the manual's type numbers are handle 3753 and charger 3757 or 3752, and the charger depends on the model bought. Opening the handle destroys the appliance, and the teardown has the motor, battery plates and motherboard soldered together.

gaps: The teardown article gives the cell as Sanyo 3.7 V, 740 mAh without naming the chemistry; Li-ion comes from the iFixit iO battery guide 136696.
The motor driver and the Bluetooth chip are named in the article text only as Texas Instruments parts; the part numbers DRV8850 and CC2640R2F appear only in the URLs of links to TI product pages.
The Cypress microcontroller, Winbond flash, Hall sensor, charging coil and OLED have no part numbers in the article, so none are claimed.

The manual is a multi-model iO manual; its charger types 3757 and 3752 depend on the model, so it is not known which goes with the torn-down handle. The charger ratings are the manual's Mexico-only block.
iFixit guide 136696 also lists a 750 mAh Braun variant of the cell; the teardown unit has the 740 mAh Sanyo cell.
One teardown unit only; later iO models may use other parts.
method: iFixit teardown article 'A Teardown Peek Inside Oral B's Seriously Connected iO Toothbrush' (Tobias Isakeit, 20 October 2020): battery, motor, chip, sensor, display, button and coil sentences; no photo caption names a chip.
iFixit guide 136696, Oral-B iO Battery Replacement: parts list 49 x 14 mm Li-ion iO batteries, 740 mAh (Sanyo item page) and 750 mAh (Braun item page).

Oral-B iO manual, ManualsLib copy 834242 (63 pages) on manualslib.mx: type numbers on page 2, Mexico-only charger block on page 46 (Portuguese), Li-ion label and end-of-life battery removal on page 16.
TI product pages for the DRV8850 (motor driver) and CC2640R2F (Bluetooth LE wireless MCU) open and name the chips; they are the pages the teardown links.

comps.spec: Sanyo cell rated 3.7 V, 740 mAh, which the teardown says can be removed by hand without tools; Li-ion per iFixit's iO battery guide 136696 (740 mAh Sanyo part)
Charger type 3752 (100-240 V ~, 50-60 Hz, 0.9 W) or type 3757 (110-130 V ~, 60 Hz, 0.9 W), from the iO manual's Mexico-only block; which type depends on the model bought
Frictionless coil motor (not a rotary motor) giving linear up-and-down motion without a cam or gear; secured by Torx 8 screws
Motor driver from Texas Instruments; the teardown links it to TI's DRV8850 product page (the part number appears only in the link)
Bluetooth wireless microcontroller from Texas Instruments; the teardown links it to TI's CC2640R2F product page (the part number appears only in the link)
Cypress microcontroller found in the teardown
Winbond flash memory chip found in the teardown
Hall effect sensor on top of the motherboard; it reads the field of a small magnet on a flexible plastic piece to sense brushing pressure
Charging coil soldered to the bottom end of the board
Motherboard; the teardown lists the Hall sensor, OLED screen, two buttons, the Texas Instruments, Cypress and Winbond chips and the charging coil as found on it
OLED screen held to the motherboard by a small adhesive strip, with its cable soldered on rather than plugged in
Two buttons found in the teardown
